title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standards for service-level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning methodologies, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling requirements, and canonical SRE runbooks. The intent is to provide a single authoritative reference for service owners and on-call engineers to keep production reliability predictable and measurable.

Scope
- Applies to all externally-facing inference endpoints, control-plane APIs, and critical supporting platform services (model cache, KV-store, scheduler, billing API).
- Not intended for ephemeral developer environments; see eng-infra docs for dev/non-prod policies.

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

Principles
- SLOs should be customer-centric: availability and latency SLOs map to user-facing impacts (generation latency, dropped requests, failed responses).
- Keep SLOs measurable and automated: source SLO measurements from production telemetry (prod metrics pipeline).
- Error budgets are the policy unit: they control rollouts, feature enablement, and emergency throttles.

Canonical SLOs (examples)
| Service | SLO | Window | Target | Owner |
|---------|-----|--------|--------|-------|
| api.generate (text-gen v1) | Successful responses (2xx) + latency p95 | 30d | 99.95% success / p95 <= 350ms | api-service-owner@redwood.com |
| chat.stream (realtime) | Stream availability & first-byte latency p50 | 7d | 99.9% availability / p50 <= 120ms | chat-service-owner@redwood.com |
| embeddings.create | Success rate | 30d | 99.99% | embeddings-team@redwood.com |
| control-plane.auth | Auth+token-issue availability | 30d | 99.99% | platform-security@redwood.com |

Error budget calculation and policy
- Error budget = 1 - SLO. For api.generate with 99.95% target over 30d, monthly error budget = 0.05% of requests.
- Burn rate: computed as observed-exceedance / remaining-budget over a lookback window (1h, 6h, 24h).
- Policies:
  1. Burn rate < 1: normal.
  2. 1 <= Burn rate < 4 for > 6 hours: service owner notified and automatic release freeze for non-critical changes.
  3. Burn rate >= 4 for 1 hour: page SRE on-call, begin mitigation runbook.
  4. Exhausted budget: hold new feature launches and scale capacity where possible; escalate to Engineering Director if >24h.

SLO Owners and Responsibilities
- Define measurement (metric, filter, and cardinality). Example: count(http_responses{route="/v1/generate"}) by (code) and latency histogram for p50/p95/p99 calculations.
- Maintain SLO dashboard and alerts.
- Run quarterly SLO review with product and customer success for high-impact services.

2) Capacity Planning

Goals
- Ensure headroom to absorb 99th percentile burst traffic without violating latency SLOs for at least 30 minutes.
- Clear runway for known events: major model releases, customer onboarding, marketing-driven usage spikes.

Capacity Sizing Methodology
1. Baseline measurement: collect peak QPS, avg token length, tokens/sec, and average GPU utilization for the last 90 days.
2. Model the throughput: tokens/sec per GPU for primary model families (e.g., redwood-7B, redwood-13B, llm-open-30B) and derive required GPU capacity for 99th percentile traffic.
3. Headroom policy: maintain 40% spare capacity (headroom) for hosted API production; Dedicated customers have contractually agreed headroom per SLA.
4. Autoscaling and burst: configure autoscaling latency-based (p95 queueing) with a cool-down of 60s and scale step of +20% per minute up to a hard cap defined by capacity pool.

Capacity Runway and Commitments
- Reserve runway = (scheduled capacity provision - baseline usage) / expected growth rate. Aim for 2-4 weeks runway for platform capacity changes.
- For Dedicated pools: follow contract commit tables in product-docs/pricing-and-packaging and ensure capacity change lead time is documented in the customer runbook.

Capacity Review Cadence and Ownership
- SRE and infra teams run a monthly capacity review: traffic trends, incident impacts attributable to capacity, open capacity tickets.
- Owners: infra-capacity@redwood.com (primary), eng-sre-lead (secondary).

3) Reliability Initiatives and Prioritization

Program structure
- Quarterly reliability roadmap aligned with SLOs: initiative -> owner -> success metric (SLO change or incident reduction).

Typical initiatives
- Prefix cache (KV) warmup to reduce cold-start p95 by 20% (owner: runtime-team).
- Model-variant fallback implementation to reduce generated-response failures during model OOM events (owner: serving-runtime).
- SLO-driven rollout automation: automatic throttle of canary traffic when error budgets are burning (owner: eng-platform).

Prioritization criteria
1. Measured SLO impact and number of customers affected.
2. Expected reduction in P1/P2 incidents per quarter.
3. Implementation cost and cross-team dependencies.

4) Incident Review Standards

Severity classification
- Sev1: Customer-visible outage affecting >5% of requests or >1 critical customer SLA. Immediate page, all-hands response.
- Sev2: Degradation affecting >0.5% of requests or partial-feature loss for major customers.
- Sev3: Minor degradation, single customer issue, or transient error.

Immediate post-incident actions
1. Ensure mitigation and restore customer-facing functionality.
2. Create an incident record in the incident tracker within 2 hours.
3. Notify customer-success and sales if customers are impacted.

Postmortem requirements (for Sev1/Sev2)
- Postmortem must be published within 7 days and include: timeline, impact statement (customer and metrics), proximate cause, root cause analysis, detection and response timelines, and action items with owners and ETA.
- Root cause must be documented with supporting logs and trace links.
- Action items: owners assigned and reviewed at weekly reliability triage until complete.

Blameless culture
- Focus on systems and process improvements. Avoid assigning blame to individuals in public postmortems.

5) Operational Tooling Requirements

Dashboards and Alerts
- Every SLO must have a dashboard: error budget remaining, burn rate (1h/6h/24h), request volume, latency histograms, and top error codes.
- Alert thresholds:
  - SLO burn rate >= 1.5 for 6 hours -> paged to service owner (informational).
  - SLO burn rate >= 4 for 1h -> SRE pager.
  - p95 latency > SLO for 10 minutes with traffic > 5% of baseline -> SRE pager.

Tracing and Debugging
- Distributed traces must include request id, model-id, GPU-id, and routing decision tags.
- Provide an SRE trace playbook with common trace patterns and filters for the runtime.

Automations and Integrations
- Auto-remediation runbooks: circuit-breaker modes that temporarily reduce model fidelity or throttle non-paid traffic when error budgets are exhausted.
- SLO automation: integration between telemetry pipeline and CI/CD to block canary promotions when error budget is below threshold.

6) Canonical SRE Runbooks (templates)

Runbook: Sev1 - Production Outage (api.generate)
1. Triage
   - Confirm: check alert context, dashboard (SLO burn rate, p95 latency), and recent deploys.
   - Assign a triage lead and note initial hypothesis in the incident tracker.
2. Immediate mitigations (within first 10 minutes)
   - If traffic spike: scale up dedicated pools (infra autoscale override) and enable burst capacity for hosted pools.
   - If increased error rate: enable model-variant fallback (toggle via feature-flag) or roll back the last deploy if root cause likely in new release.
   - If OOM on GPU: reduce concurrency per GPU (runtime config) to prevent cascading failures.
3. Communication
   - Status page: post initial incident message within 15 minutes with impact, services affected, and mitigation steps.
   - Pager and Slack incident channel: update every 30 minutes until recovery.
4. Recovery and verification
   - Validate recovery via SLO dashboard and real customer request sampling.
   - Gradually scale down emergency capacity using the same steps reversed and verify latency stability for 30 minutes.
5. Post-incident
   - Kick off postmortem and attach logs/traces.

Runbook: Sev2 - Partial Degradation
- Follow triage steps; if mitigation is less disruptive, prefer traffic shaping and rate-limiting.
- Document temporary configuration changes and schedule follow-up engineering fix.

Escalation paths
- On-call SRE -> Senior SRE -> SRE Lead -> Eng Director -> CTO depending on duration, customer impact, and contract SLAs.

Runbook checklist (minimum)
- Incident created in tracker with severity and timeline.
- SLO dashboard link posted.
- Pager acknowledged and triage lead assigned.
- Immediate mitigation executed or safe rollback validated.
- Customer-facing comms sent.

7) Ownership and Roles

- Service Owner: owns SLO definition, measurements, and reliability roadmap for the service.
- On-call SRE: executes runbooks, triage incidents, and coordinates mitigations.
- Infra/Capacity Owners: responsible for pool scaling and long-term capacity changes.
- Eng Platform: implements automation for rollouts and SLO gating.
- Customer Success: notified for any incident impacting paying customers; coordinates postmortem outreach.

Rotation and Escalation
- On-call rotations are weekly. Primary and secondary rota maintained in the oncall-and-incident-response folder.
- Pager duty policies: 1st pager for burn rate + p95 alerts; 2nd pager if mitigation fails for >30 minutes.

Appendices

A. Example alert (Prometheus-style)
ALERT SLOBurnRateHigh
IF (slo_burn_rate{service="api.generate",window="1h"} > 4)
FOR 1m
LABELS { severity="page" }
ANNOTATIONS { runbook="/confluence/eng-sre/sre-slos-capacity-and-runbooks-2026-03-04", summary="SLO burn rate for api.generate > 4 (1h)" }

B. Example commands and quick checks
- Check recent deploys: git log -n 5 origin/main -- services/api | cat
- Tail errors: curl -sS https://observability/api/logs?service=api.generate&level=error | jq .
- Rollback deploy: ./deploy rollback --service api --to-revision <sha>

C. Runbook maintenance
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly or after any Sev1 that triggers the runbook.
- Ownership must be reassigned if the service owner changes.
